\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कृते} (kṛte)}{कृते (kṛte)}]{\sk{कृते} (kṛte) — for the sake of}

\label{lesson:SA-C241-krte}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for daily, then the Sanskrit for constantly, always.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कृते}}
\textbf{\sk{कृते}} — \emph{kṛte} — \textquotedblleft{}for the sake of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kṛte} comes from \emph{kṛta}, \textquotedblleft{}done\textquotedblright{}, the past participle of the root √kṛ, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} (MW); it is its locative. \textquotedblleft{}In the doing of\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}for the sake of\textquotedblright{}; \emph{mama kṛte} is \textquotedblleft{}for me\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṛte}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kṛte}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for daily, then the Sanskrit for constantly, always, then say \emph{kṛte} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{येन} (yena)}{येन (yena)}]{\sk{येन} (yena) — by which, so that}

\label{lesson:SA-C241-yena}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for constantly, always, then the Sanskrit for for the sake of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{येन}}
\textbf{\sk{येन}} — \emph{yena} — \textquotedblleft{}by which, so that\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yena} comes from the relative pronoun stem \emph{ya-}, \textquotedblleft{}which\textquotedblright{}, as its instrumental (MW): \textquotedblleft{}by which\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}so that\textquotedblright{}. It pairs with \emph{tena}, \textquotedblleft{}by that\textquotedblright{}, from the next lesson.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{तेन} (tena)}{तेन (tena)}]{\sk{तेन} (tena) — by that, therefore}

\label{lesson:SA-C241-tena}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for for the sake of, then the Sanskrit for by which.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{तेन}}
\textbf{\sk{तेन}} — \emph{tena} — \textquotedblleft{}by that, therefore\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tena} is the instrumental of the pronoun stem \emph{ta-}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, whose neuter is \emph{tad} (MW). The stem is inherited from Indo-European: MW compares Greek \emph{to}, \textquotedblleft{}the\textquotedblright{}, and Gothic \emph{thata}, the cousin of English \emph{that}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{यत्} (yat)}{यत् (yat)}]{\sk{यत्} (yat) — that (introducing a clause)}

\label{lesson:SA-C241-yat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for by which, then the Sanskrit for by that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{यत्}}
\textbf{\sk{यत्}} — \emph{yat} — \textquotedblleft{}that (introducing a clause)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yat} is the neuter form of the relative pronoun stem \emph{ya-}, \textquotedblleft{}which, what\textquotedblright{} (MW). Used at the head of a clause it means \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, the way English \emph{that} introduces \textquotedblleft{}he said that ...\textquotedblright{}. Hindi \emph{jo}, \textquotedblleft{}who, which\textquotedblright{}, comes from the same stem (CDIAL 10391).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{परन्तु} (parantu)}{परन्तु (parantu)}]{\sk{परन्तु} (parantu) — however, but}

\label{lesson:SA-C241-parantu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for by that, then the Sanskrit for that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{परन्तु}}
\textbf{\sk{परन्तु}} — \emph{parantu} — \textquotedblleft{}however, but\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{parantu} is built on \emph{param}, \textquotedblleft{}beyond, further, but\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{para}, \textquotedblleft{}far, other\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{tu}, \textquotedblleft{}but, on the other hand\textquotedblright{} (MW). Two words for \textquotedblleft{}but\textquotedblright{} joined into one.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for by that, then the Sanskrit for that, then say \emph{parantu} again
